body:
First fanout PR: #1977 for BUG-1283 — ready for your gate, with two things I want a reviewer to look at and one I cannot judge

I directed this implementation, so my read of it is compromised by exactly the mechanism we put in the discipline pack this afternoon: I know what it is for and will check whether it matches that purpose. Handing it over rather than forming a verdict.

WHAT IT DOES. +104/-5 across three files. The test fix is clean and is what the spec asked for: `failed_pull_rebase_aborts_and_restores_branch` now asserts `git show HEAD:shared.yaml` instead of `read_to_string` on the working-tree file, which removes the autocrlf variable rather than papering over it. The Windows-only failure cannot recur through that path. It did NOT cfg the test away, which was your explicit prohibition.

TWO THINGS FOR A REVIEWER.

First, the assertion now compares against "value: local" with no trailing newline, where the old one compared against "value: local\n". That is presumably the git-helper trimming its stdout, and it is plausible — but it is the exact class of byte-level assumption that caused the original bug, and I would want someone who did not write it to confirm the helper actually trims rather than assume it.

Second, and this is the one that matters: running the widened ratchet against the existing tree surfaced 22 pre-existing instances of the two new shapes, and they were added to scripts/portability-allowlist.txt as baseline debt rather than fixed. I checked before objecting — that file already carried about 169 entries, so baselining is the established pattern here and not something the agent invented. Out-of-scope-for-this-spec is a defensible call.

But it means the two new rules fire on nothing today, so they are unproven against real code, and if any of those 22 is a genuine Windows defect it is now permanently silenced by the mechanism meant to catch it. The agent did prove the rules work by writing a throwaway fixture containing both shapes and watching the script flag them, then deleting it — which is better evidence than nothing, and weaker than a real hit. Your call whether the 22 need triaging before or after this merges; I would not block on it, but I would not let it disappear either.

WHAT I CANNOT JUDGE. The spec's acceptance includes verifying by a cross-platform.yml dispatch rather than by assertion. The agent did not dispatch the Windows nightly and said so plainly rather than claiming it. That gate is yours or the operator's — and it is the only criterion that actually proves the Windows failure is gone, since everything else was verified on Linux.

Reported verification I did not re-run: cargo test -p aida-core git_ops 50 passed, cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, bash scripts/check-portability.sh exit 0.

One cosmetic thing: the branch is worktree-agent-a607e7f47f9774e77 rather than the bug-1283 convention, because the fanout lane names branches after the agent. Functional — the commit trailer carries the spec — but it will look odd in the branch list, and if the fanout becomes routine it is worth deciding whether these should be renamed at PR time.

The other two lanes, BUG-1285 and TASK-1297, are still running.
